A region is bounded by semicircular arcs constructed on the side of a square whose sides measure $ 2/\pi $, as shown. What is the perimeter of this region?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the center of the figure is a square, and on each of the four sides of the square, a semicircle is constructed outward; the four semicircular arcs together form the outer boundary of the shaded region. The sides of the square are only the diameter lines of the semicircles, located inside or at the boundary, and do not belong to the external perimeter. Reasoning: The side length of the square is 2/π, so the diameter of each semicircle is 2/π, and the radius is 1/π. The arc length of one semicircle is πr = π·(1/π) = 1. There are 4 such external semicircular arcs in total, therefore the total perimeter is 4·1 = 4.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the outer boundary consists of four congruent semicircular arcs, one based on each side of the central square. From the text, each diameter is the square side, 2/pi. Instead of summing four semicircles one by one, group the four semicircles as two complete circles of diameter 2/pi.
